trials.name: DIAN-TU-001
trials.population: Individuals at risk for or with a type of early onset Alzheimer's disease caused by a genetic mutation
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in the DIAN-Multivariate Cognitive Endpoint (DIAN-MCE)
trials.results_summary: Neither gantenerumab nor solanezumab met the primary cognitive endpoint of slowing clinical decline, despite gantenerumab showing significant reductions in amyloid plaques.

trials.name: EMERGE (221AD302)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score at Week 78
trials.results_summary: The trial was terminated early for futility, but subsequent post-hoc analyses indicated a 22% reduction in clinical decline for the high-dose group on the CDR-SB.

trials.name: ENGAGE (221AD301)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score at Week 78
trials.results_summary: The trial was terminated early after a futility analysis and failed to show a significant treatment effect on cognitive decline, conflicting with the positive signal seen in EMERGE.

trials.name: Study 201
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Alzheimer's Disease Composite Score (ADCOMS) at Month 12
trials.results_summary: The trial did not meet its primary 12-month ADCOMS endpoint, but at 18 months, the highest dose demonstrated robust amyloid clearance and a 47% reduction in clinical decline on ADCOMS.

trials.name: Clarity AD
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline in the CDR-SB at 18 Months
trials.results_summary: Met its primary endpoint by slowing cognitive decline by 27% on the CDR-SB over 18 months compared to placebo, alongside significant amyloid plaque clearance.

related_evidence.description: Primary results of the DIAN-TU trial showing lack of cognitive benefit for gantenerumab and solanezumab.
Results of the lecanemab Phase 2b trial (Study 201) demonstrating a 47% slowing of clinical decline at 18 months on ADCOMS.
Primary publication of the Phase 3 EMERGE and ENGAGE trials for aducanumab.
Primary publication of the Phase 3 Clarity AD trial for lecanemab showing a 27% reduction in cognitive decline.

evidence_assessment: The clinical trial record strongly supports the document's central premise that the deterministic amyloid cascade hypothesis is insufficient to fully explain sporadic AD. Anti-amyloid therapies consistently show robust target engagement (amyloid clearance) but yield modest or inconsistent cognitive benefits. Aducanumab's ENGAGE trial failed entirely, while EMERGE showed only a 22% reduction in decline on the CDR-SB. The cited 47% reduction for lecanemab comes from a Phase 2b secondary endpoint, and the subsequent Phase 3 Clarity AD trial demonstrated a more modest 27% reduction. These findings corroborate the authors' argument that a substantial proportion of clinical progression in AD occurs independently of amyloid-beta, validating the need for a probabilistic model that accounts for compounding genetic and environmental factors.
discrepancies: The document claims lecanemab slowed cognitive decline by 47%. This refers to the 18-month secondary endpoint of the Phase 2b trial (NCT01767311). The subsequent, fully powered Phase 3 Clarity AD trial (NCT03887455), which reported results after this paper was published, showed a more modest 27% reduction in decline. However, this discrepancy effectively strengthens the authors' broader conclusion that the majority of disease progression (over 70% in Phase 3) remains independent of Aβ.
